sentences.text: Lusovenator is a genus containing only one known species, Lusovenator santosi. It belongs to the group of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaurs, a lineage of large carnivores.

The genus name combines 'Lusitania', the ancient name for Portugal, and 'venator', meaning hunter, to translate as 'Portuguese hunter'. The species name 'santos' honors the discoverer, José Joaquim dos Santos.

The holotype specimen, which is the specific fossil the species is based on, was discovered in the 1980s by José Joaquim dos Santos. He donated the fossil collection to the Sociedade de História Natural approximately thirty years after finding it.
This holotype consists of a partial postcranial skeleton including vertebrae, ribs, and pelvic fragments, thought to represent a juvenile individual.

The holotype was initially described and classified within Allosauroidea in 2017. A neotype was described in 2019, and both the holotype and neotype were subsequently placed within Carcharodontosauria. The species name Lusovenator santosi was formally named and described in 2020.
Phylogenetic analysis places Lusovenator within Carcharodontosauria but outside the families Carcharodontosauridae and Neovenatoridae.
Fossils of this animal have been found in the Lourinhã Formation in present-day Portugal. It lived between 152.21 and 143.1 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
A 2024 study by Cau suggests Lusovenator belongs to the family Carcharodontosauridae, grouping it with Sauroniops, Veterupristisaurus, Eocarcharia, and Concavenator.
